messages:
maria-ops: FYI escalation from OpenMaps — starting ~2026-03-14T00:10Z they're seeing 5xx on POST /v1/generate. They expect 429 when quota exceeded but instead get 500/502 spikes. Customer reported high error rate and provided request_id rq_0a1b2c3d. Repro steps below, ticket attached.

jamal-support: paste of customer's repro curl:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"hello"}'
```
response snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d

{"error":"internal server error"}
```

alex-sre: Thanks. Can you paste the full request_id and approximate UTC ts? Need to check gateway logs + quota service traces. Also: is the 5xx returned from our gateway (envoy) or from quota-service upstream?

maria-ops: request_id rq_0a1b2c3d -> trace span shows quota-lookup call returned deadline exceeded around 00:10:12Z. From gateway logs:
```
2026-03-14T00:10:12.123Z INFO proxy request_id=rq_0a1b2c3d upstream=quota-lookup status=504 latency_ms=3002
2026-03-14T00:10:12.124Z ERROR proxy request_id=rq_0a1b2c3d responding 502 to client
```
Note: quota-lookup should return 429 for limit exceed, not 5xx.

alex-sre: Initial theory: route misconfiguration causing requests to be routed to a stale/legacy quota cluster that is unhealthy -> connection resets/timeouts -> envoys translating to 5xx. I'm seeing a recent canary deploy that changed route tags. Querying local admin routes now.

alex-sre: admin check snippet:
```bash
# on one of the fronting pods
kubectl exec -n infra proxy-frontend-0 -c envoy -- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9901/config_dump | jq '.configs[] | select(.dynamic_resources != null) | .dynamic_resources' | grep quota-legacy || true
```
Found route pointing at cluster "quota-legacy" for /v1/generate. Route timeout = 3s.

jamal-support: That matches timeline — canary rollout started 00:05Z and had tag rewrite for quota -> quota-legacy temporarily. Customer traffic likely hit the canary hostpool.

sre-oncall: For immediate mitigation we should map validation/quota failures to 4xx at the gateway when upstream returns 5xx from quota service, rather than bubbling 5xx to customers. Can we add a quick mapping rule? Also rollback canary if needed.

alex-sre: Agreed. Quick mitigation plan:
1) Patch envoy route to point back to quota-primary (hotfix).
2) Add a response classification rule: if upstream cluster==quota-* and status>=500 and header X-Quota-Error present then map -> 429.
3) Deploy route change to small subset then global.

Patch command applied (hotfix):
```bash
kubectl -n infra exec proxy-frontend-0 -c envoy -- bash -lc "cat >/tmp/route-patch.json <<'PATCH'\n{\n  \"route\":{\n    \"match\":{\"prefix\":\"/v1/generate\"},\n    \"route\":{\"cluster\":\"quota-primary\",\"timeout\":\"6s\"},\n    \"response_headers_to_add\":[{\"header\":{\"key\":\"x-quota-fallback\",\"value\":\"true\"}}]\n  }\n}\nPATCH\nkubectl cp /tmp/route-patch.json proxy-frontend-0:/tmp/route-patch.json -n infra && \
# trigger config reload path (internal tool)\n/proxy/bin/reload-config --file /tmp/route-patch.json"
```
Applied to 3 frontends as test.

ops-bot: metric snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/errors?from=2026-03-14T00:00:00Z&to=2026-03-14T01:00:00Z -> 5xx spike at 00:10 (p50->p95 latency increase), quota-lookup 504 count +3800 in 5m window.

maria-ops: After patch to quota-primary on subset, customer reports error rate dropped to near-zero for their sessions. We rolled patch global at 00:35Z.

alex-sre: Root cause summary (prelim): canary rollout introduced a route tag mismatch that pointed /v1/generate to a legacy quota cluster (quota-legacy) that did not have healthy upstreams for the new auth header format. That cluster returned timeouts/connection resets. Envoy translated these to 5xx instead of 429 because the legacy cluster did not implement quota semantics.

sre-oncall: Postmortem actions:
- Revert/remove temporary tag rewrite in canary pipeline. (done)
- Add response mapping rule so gateway maps known quota upstream failures to 429 with clear body and "x-quota-fallback" header.
- Add canary gating: route tag validation step during rollout to ensure cluster exists + healthy upstreams.
- Add integration test that simulates quota-lookup timeouts and asserts gateway returns 429.

jamal-support: Customer notified, they accepted the mitigation and asked for timeline for permanent fix. I'll coordinate SLA credit if needed.

maria-ops: Closing thread once postmortem doc is up. Thanks y'all. :tada:

deploy-bot: Deployed patch to frontends @ 2026-03-14T00:27Z (3 pods), global rollout @ 2026-03-14T00:35Z.

ops-bot: Final metrics (post-rollout): quota-lookup 504s down 98%, customer 5xx error rate returned to baseline.
